comparison: For a chosen regular conditional law of real treatment A given L, evaluate its CDF at a and take the real derivative in a; do the same for the marginal law of A to obtain varpi_0. The source assumes both densities exist. condDistrib provides a conditional-law version for a nonempty standard Borel output under a finite probability measure, and deriv expresses the displayed derivative with zero fallback outside differentiability. Keep the density/existence assumptions and establish that the chosen derivative represents the conditional or marginal law with respect to Lebesgue measure; mere almost-everywhere CDF differentiability does not rule out a singular component. Conditional-law identities are almost everywhere in L and do not determine all covariate-support values without selecting the required version. The continuous-treatment propensity is a density, may exceed one, and is not the binary event probability P(A=1|L). No uniform positivity or smoothness is supplied by this definition alone.
